scope: Read-only source and raw session metadata inspection. No user session writes, no original bodies, tool commands or credentials in this receipt. Raw session rows were parsed for metadata; no claim of independent transcript-chain authentication.

findings.finding: appendSessionInputWithReceipt stores clientMessageId and inputDigest on user_message.data, while headless-stream inserts only role/content into the live array. The strict canonical projection retains the two fields, so the first live-prefix comparison differs for accepted receipt-bearing input.
Both file replay and legacy event-array host replay must use the same conversation projection; receipt lookup/deduplication must keep the authenticated raw event unchanged.

History origins hash all message fields and decode direct events and snapshots. A store-only projection change can lose fork/rewind history origin mappings. Apply equivalent message projection at history origins and cover receipt-bearing historical compact/checkpoint snapshots.
Page v1/v2 rows and Markdown render role/content only. Raw event export and receipt lookup should continue retaining receipt metadata.

Installed 117 and 0459 have identical LF-normalized headless-stream, provider-stream-state, message-roles, jsonl-session-store, session-message-provenance, session-tool-round, live-compaction, message-adapter and session-runtime-retention. agent-core differs only in the Ollama fetch transport import and two calls; no Volcengine/SSE/Git difference.

recommendation: Project the two known receipt metadata fields out of conversation messages consistently, after preserving raw authority evidence. Do not skip prefix checks, do not resample/drop concurrent user input, do not remove fields from raw receipt events or loosen malformed-message checks.

limitations: Source and pure projection comparison establish the deterministic mismatch condition. The installed process raw error code is not available; this receipt alone does not assert which exception was emitted by that terminated process.
